report:
## Conclusion

The evidence suggests a **modest but plausible inverse association** between moderate dark chocolate/chocolate consumption and stroke risk — but this falls short of proving that chocolate *causes* reduced stroke risk.

**What the evidence shows:**
- Multiple prospective cohort studies and meta-analyses have found that higher chocolate consumption (particularly dark chocolate, ~3–6 servings/week) is associated with lower risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and cardiovascular disease overall compared to low/no consumption, with a dose-response relationship that plateaus at moderate intake ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6643/18/4/636), [mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6643/9/7/688)). A large meta-analysis in *Heart* similarly found chocolate consumption inversely associated with CVD risk ([heart.bmj.com](https://heart.bmj.com/content/105/1/49)).
- A prospective cohort in *Neurology* found chocolate consumption associated with lower stroke risk in men, reinforced by meta-analysis of prior studies ([neurology.org](https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0b013e31826aacfa)).
- A 2024 Mendelian randomization study specifically testing dark chocolate intake found evidence supporting a causal reduction in essential hypertension risk, lending biological plausibility, though its stroke-specific causal findings are less definitive ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10781976/)).
- Proposed mechanisms include cocoa flavanols improving endothelial function, lowering blood pressure, and inhibiting platelet activation — all plausible stroke-protective pathways, though mostly demonstrated in short-term physiological studies rather than long-term outcome trials ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3022066/)).

**Caveats:** Observational associations are subject to confounding (e.g., chocolate consumers may have healthier diets/lifestyles), and benefits do not scale with higher intake, given chocolate's sugar/fat content.

**Bottom line:** Moderate dark chocolate consumption is associated with modestly lower stroke risk, with plausible supporting mechanisms, but causal proof remains incomplete.
